title: Monthly sea-level differences had lower lag-one correlation than mouth levels in Chesapeake in 1991-2025
abstract: We tested whether inland-minus-mouth sea-level differences retain less monthly memory than mouth levels in two US estuaries. We used four NOAA gauges in 1991-2025, with 407 common months and 399 adjacent-month pairs. After removal of monthly seasonal means and a linear trend, the lag-one correlation difference was -0.243 in Chesapeake and +0.106 in Delaware. Chesapeake had conditional 95% three-year block limits of -0.374 to -0.099. Its two-site adjusted limits were -0.390 to -0.083. The planned mean across both estuaries was -0.068, with limits of -0.166 to +0.045. Thus there was no clear common decrease. Checks for trend form, inferred values, period and block length retained the negative Chesapeake contrast. This is a diagnostic benchmark, not proof of faster physical recovery or forecast value. Subtraction, measurement noise, chosen gauges, missing months and conditional uncertainty limit interpretation. Code, provenance, annual statistical summaries, resampling draws, an arithmetic audit and a figure are included.
